data.narrative:
Telexistence is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jin Tomioka and Ken Tomoyose, having raised $170M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparables universe of nine private firms and one public company (277810.KQ) operating in the same sector and stage.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $170M raised as a proxy base value and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying a valuation of $323M. The peer-median method references three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), and Dexterity ($1.6B)—yielding a median valuation of $1.8B with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $275M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.0B across both methods. The wide spread reflects material uncertainty around whether Telexistence's revenue scale, customer traction, and technology maturity align with the lower stage-progression estimate or the elevated peer median. Critical variables for narrowing this range include current-period revenue run rate, customer concentration, and gross margins relative to the comparables set.
